text: rwb-deviation serves the deviation state of a page of cases on GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviation-flags with the caseId query repeated, one to the page bound, read only and one hop; the operation is not a row of the Ownership Map and its exact form is fixed at the contract review of RWB-P2-E2033-CON.
why: The list of this legacy key needs the deviation state of a page and the Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations and no read, so the read is declared here with a gap rather than invented as an owner row.
read: Ownership Map API rows for S8; Architecture v5 slides 13, 41 and 45; TSD S8 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13 and R9.
impact: One additional read operation on the service base; a change of path or field names is a contract change and not a code change.

text: deviationOpen on the case and queue list stays rwb-case's field deviation_open (DF-CAS-019), read through the case contract of RWB-P2-E2033-CON, and the answer of this story is the evidence beside it; the two are asserted equal on every page and neither value is copied into the other service's schema.
why: The flag belongs to the case owner by the Ownership Map while the deviation rows belong to S8, so the fact exists twice and the split must say which answer is the record and which is the evidence.
read: Ownership Map tables recovery_case (owner P3) and deviation (owner S8); TSD S8 T3.1; legacy RWB-E2-033 AC1, AC2 and BR4; RWB-P2-E2033-APP section 7.
impact: One agreement test per page fixture; a drift between the two answers fails the build before SIT.

text: The platform contracts that DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 name arrive with the service template, so the metadata row Depends on (build) stays None as the Work Package fixes it and Contract dependencies stays RWB-P2-E2033-CON; the authorise, parameters and reference-data contracts consumed by this read are class C in fact and are not written into either row.
why: The plan gives this secondary slice an empty H row and one C row, while the DP table of the pattern set adds six platform H dependencies and three cross-service C dependencies.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; split plan story line RWB-S8-E2033-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; sibling story RWB-S8-E1062-APP section 13.
confirm: Solution architect; platform library owner (RWB-PLT-E1042, RWB-PLT-E1043, RWB-PLT-E1037, RWB-PLT-E1047, RWB-PLT-E1044, RWB-PLT-N001)
impact: Ready to start stays Day 1; the platform contracts are tracked by their own stories and not by this lane.

text: The number of case ids one request may carry is the case-list page bound read as a parameter row of rwb-case, 1 to 200 in the legacy validation, with the version in force; an empty request is refused with MSG-GEN-001 and a request above the bound with MSG-GEN-002, and no bound is written in code.
why: The legacy story validates the page size against 1 to 200 and reads it as a validation rule, while DP-06 and the legacy guardrail require every changeable value to be a parameter row.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 3, X2, AC7 and section 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06; Ownership Map parameter_value (owner P3) and API GET /admin/parameters.
confirm: Business lead for the bound; rwb-case parameter owner (RWB-P3-E1042-CON)
impact: A change of bound is a data change in rwb-case and no release of this service.

text: The text of MSG-GEN-006 is not printed by any source read for this slice, so the placeholder stands in section 14 and the wording is taken from the platform Error and Message Standard at build time; the identifier, the HTTP status 503 and the use of the message for a consumed contract that does not answer inside the budget are fixed here.
why: FSD S8 names MSG-GEN-006 in its exception flows with the name of the module and prints no text, and an invented sentence would be a business value of this story.
read: FSD S8 A2.2.4.3, A2.6.4.3 and A2.9.4.3; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 14; Template and Rules v1 R9.
confirm: Platform message catalogue owner; solution architect
impact: The message identifier and status are stable; only the wording is filled from the catalogue.

text: LOV-DEVIATION and LOV-RAISED-BY are read at the version in force through the reference-data contract of rwb-case, whose path and field names are fixed in RWB-P3-E1043-CON because no source names them; the codes of the version in force and not a list of this service decide which codes the projection covers.
why: DP-07 moves reference data and lists of values to rwb-case, the legacy story named its lists without a path, and the Ownership Map carries no reference-data GET row.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and R3 default rulings; TSD S8 T3.2; Ownership Map lov_value and reference_row (owner P3); legacy RWB-E2-033 section 8 BR6.
impact: Adding or retiring a code is a data change in rwb-case; no code is a constant of this module.

text: The twelve legacy test cases carry no level, so one is assigned per case: legacy System maps to Component for a single-service half, legacy Access maps to Component, and a case whose behaviour belongs to the composed page or the export is listed with no criterion here.
why: The legacy table publishes only the ID, the coverage and the data, and the split gives each case one service to run against.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 16; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s16; sibling story RWB-S8-E1062-APP section 16.
impact: The same test IDs run in one service or in the integration harness; no case is lost and none is duplicated.

text: pauseRequired is the projection of the open deviation rows of a case and of the resume rule that a case returns only when all its deviations are cleared; the read does not evaluate the DEV package, because DP-04 is not in this story's pattern set, and the pause and resume themselves are executed by the raise, route and clear steps in DeviationWorkflow.
why: R-DEV-01, R-DEV-09 and R-DEV-18 are rule rows of the DEV package, while the plan's pattern list for this slice holds DP-01, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-13, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 and no embedded Drools read.
read: FSD S8 A2.2.3.1, A2.6.3.1 and A2.9.3.1; TSD S8 T4; legacy RWB-E2-033 BR4 and AC2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04.
impact: The list shows the paused state from the rows alone; a change of the resume rule is a change of the raise and clear stories and of one shared test.

text: This story adds one step to the per-service Flyway sequence of rwb_deviation: a read-only view v_deviation_flag over deviation with one index on the case and the open predicate; no business table, column or constraint is added and no migration of this service touches another schema. The view and index names are this story's design choice.
why: DP-15 is in the pattern list of the legacy key while the read copies nothing, and no source names a view over deviation.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15; TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.3; Ownership Map tables deviation (owner S8) and the four platform library objects.
impact: One migration file in the service's own sequence; the schema keeps one business table for the deviation service.

text: The deviation column of the Excel extract carries the same answer as the page, read for the rows the export covers, while the file itself is built and written by RWB-P2-E2033-APP and no file is produced by this service.
why: The legacy story writes the ageing and clock columns into one file inside the monolith, and the split leaves the file with the composition while the deviation value stays with its owner.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-033 flow steps 9 and 10, AC3 and section 12; RWB-P2-E2033-CON 12.1 and 12.9; Template and Rules v1 R5.4.
impact: One answer serves two surfaces; the file carries no copied deviation row and no personal field.
